'''STEAM''' ('''science, technology, engineering, art, and mathematics''') '''education''' is an expanded approach to teaching [[science, technology, engineering, and mathematics]] (STEM), an interdisciplinary and integrated teaching method for those four subjects. STEAM expands on STEM education by including [[the arts]].<ref name="sciam">{{cite web|last1=Pomeroy|first1=Steven Ross|title=From STEM to STEAM: Science and Art Go Hand-in-Hand|url=https://blogs.scientificamerican.com/guest-blog/from-stem-to-steam-science-and-the-arts-go-hand-in-hand/|website=blogs.scientificamerican.com|publisher=[[Scientific American]]|access-date=17 November 2016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Jones |first=Elena |date=2022-01-11 |title=STEM Vs STEAM: Making Room For The Arts |url=https://spiraltoys.com/stem-vs-steam-making-room-for-the-arts/ |access-date=2022-05-02 |website=Spiral Toys |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="huffpo">{{cite web|last1=Eger|first1=John|title=National Science Foundation Slowly Turning STEM to STEAM|url=https://huffingtonpost.com/john-m-eger/national-science-foundati_b_868449.html|website=www.huffingtonpost.com|date=31 May 2011|publisher=[[Huffington Post]]|access-date=17 November 2016}}</ref> STEAM programs aim to teach students [[innovation]], to [[critical thinking|think critically]], and to use engineering or technology in imaginative designs or creative approaches to real-world problems while building on students' mathematics and science base.

==Program examples==
Examples of state-based STEAM programs, guidance or related resources in the United States include:<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dell'Erba |first=Mary |title=Policy Considerations for STEAM Education |url=https://files.eric.ed.gov/fulltext/ED595045.pdf}}</ref>
* [[Ohio]]'s ''Quality Model for STEM and STEAM Schools''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Quality Model for STEM and STEAM Schools {{!}} Ohio Department of Education and Workforce |url=https://education.ohio.gov/Topics/STEM-Science-Technology-Engineering-and-Mathem/Quality-Model-for-STEM-and-STEAM-Schools |access-date=2025-01-11 |website=education.ohio.gov}}</ref> By [[law of Ohio|Ohio statute]], a STEAM school is designated as a type of STEM school.<ref>{{Cite report |title=Ohio Coal Research Consortium fifth year final reports summary, September 1, 1994--February 29, 1996 |date=1996-12-01 |publisher=Office of Scientific and Technical Information (OSTI) |doi=10.2172/442052 |osti=442052 }}</ref>
* In May 2014, [[Rhode Island]] created the ''STEAM Now Coalition''.<ref>RI-STEAM-Now-Coalition_1pager_Oct2015-REV.pdf</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=RI STEAM Now Coalition – RI STEAM Center |url=https://www.risteamcenter.org/coalition/ |access-date=2025-01-12 |language=en-US}}</ref>
* In 2017, [[Nevada]] enacted legislation for the creation of a State Seal of STEM Program and a State Seal of STEAM Program. The STEAM seal is given to students who have "high level of proficiency in science, technology, engineering, the arts and mathematics."<ref>{{Cite web |title=STEM-STEAM Seal Subcommittee |url=https://osit.nv.gov/STEM/STEM-STEAM_Seal_Subcommittee/ |access-date=2025-01-11 |website=osit.nv.gov}}</ref>
* In [[South Carolina]], the South Carolina State Department of Education created the South Carolina STEAM Implementation Continuum "to provide statewide guidance and consistency with regard to STEAM implementation".<ref>{{Cite web |title=South Carolina STEAM Implementation Continuum – Center for Standards, Assessment, and Accountability |url=https://csaa.wested.org/resource/south-carolina-steam-implementation-continuum/ |access-date=2025-01-12 |website=csaa.wested.org}}</ref>
*[[Georgia Tech|Georgia Institute of Technology]] (Georgia Tech) in collaboration with its Center for Education Integrating Science, Mathematics and Computing (CEISMC) created the GoSTEAM program. GoSTEAM is a program that integrates art and music into STEM focused curriculum for students in the [[K–12]] ([[kindergarten]] to twelfth grade studies).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Home {{!}} Georgia Tech - CEISMC - Center for Education Integrating Science, Mathematics and Computing |url=https://ceismc.gatech.edu/ |access-date=2025-01-12 |website=ceismc.gatech.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=GoSTEAM – K-12 STEAM Learning |url=https://steam.ceismc.gatech.edu/ |access-date=2025-01-12 |language=en-US}}</ref>

== J-STEAM ==
The Journal of STEAM Education (J-STEAM) is a free and [[Open access|open-access]] journal that is [[Peer review|peer-reviewed]] by an international team of reviewers. It is an online publication and is published by the STEAM Education Research Association. The journal publishes articles from a range of topics in [[educational research]] and related disciplines. As J-STEAM, it has an emphasis on the integration of STEAM topics, namely science, technology, engineering, art, and mathematics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=J-STEAM - Journal of STEAM Education {{!}} ISRES - International Society for Research in Education and Science |url=https://www.isres.org/j-steam-journal-of-steam-education-32.html |access-date=2025-01-12 |website=www.isres.org}}</ref>

== STEAM in children's media ==

*[[Sesame Street|''Sesame Street''{{'}}s]] 43rd season continues to focus on STEM but finds ways to integrate art. They state: "This helps make learning STEM concepts relevant and enticing to young children by highlighting how artists use STEM knowledge to enhance their art or solve problems. It also provides context for the importance of STEM knowledge in careers in the arts (e.g. musician, painter, sculptor, and dancer)."<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.gpb.org/blogs/passion-for-learning/2012/08/24/sesame-street-new-season-focuses-on-s-t-e-a-m|title=Sesame Street: New Season Focuses on S.T.E.A.M.|last=Jean-Louis|first=Rosemary|date=24 August 2012|website=gpb.org|access-date=30 October 2019}}</ref>
*[[MGA Entertainment]] created a S.T.E.A.M.-based franchise called [[Project Mc2|Project Mc{{sup|2}}]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite press release|url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/november-8-is-national-stemsteam-day-300173696.html|title=November 8 Is National S.T.E.M./S.T.E.A.M. Day|last=Entertainment|first=M. G. A.|website=www.prnewswire.com|language=en|access-date=2019-11-06}}</ref>

== Criticism of STEAM ==
STEM subjects can incorporate art to assist teaching STEM, where art is a tool for STEM in the form of STEAM education. However, some criticism holds that art and STEM subjects should be of equal value in the education process.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Mejias |first1=Sam |last2=Thompson |first2=Naomi |last3=Sedas |first3=Raul Mishael |last4=Rosin |first4=Mark |last5=Soep |first5=Elisabeth |last6=Peppler |first6=Kylie |last7=Roche |first7=Joseph |last8=Wong |first8=Jen |last9=Hurley |first9=Mairéad |last10=Bell |first10=Philip |last11=Bevan |first11=Bronwyn |date=2021 |title=The trouble with STEAM and why we use it anyway |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/sce.21605 |journal=Science Education |language=en |volume=105 |issue=2 |pages=209–231 |doi=10.1002/sce.21605 |bibcode=2021SciEd.105..209M |issn=1098-237X|hdl=2262/96427 |hdl-access=free }}</ref>

== Other uses of STEAM ==
*Meanings of the "A" that have been promoted include [[agriculture]], [[architecture]], and [[applied mathematics]].<ref name="vt.edu">{{cite web|url=http://www.vtnews.vt.edu/articles/2012/07/073112-uged-steampartnership.html|title=Virginia Tech and Virginia STEAM Academy form strategic partnership to meet critical education needs|date=31 July 2012|work=Virginia Tech News}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web | url=http://stemtosteam.org/ |title = Public Engagement &#124; Academics &#124; RISD}}</ref>
*The [[Rhode Island School of Design]] has a STEM to STEAM program and at one point maintained an interactive map that showed global STEAM initiatives.<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.risd.edu/news/for-press/press-releases/rhode-island-school-design-launches-steam-map-demonstrate-global | title = Rhode Island School of Design Launches STEAM Map to Demonstrate Global Activity and Support for the Movement | date = 7 May 2014 | access-date=23 February 2023}}</ref>  Relevant organizations were able to add themselves to the map, though it is no longer available at the location stated in press releases.<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.risd.edu/news/stories/steam-map-debuts-capitol-hill |title = STEAM Map Debuts on Capitol Hill | date=21 May 2014 | access-date=23 February 2023}}</ref> [[John Maeda]], (2008 to 2013 president of [[Rhode Island School of Design]]) has been a champion in bringing the initiative to the political forums of educational policy.
*Some programs offer STEAM from a base focus like mathematics and science.<ref name="edweek">{{cite journal|last1=Jolly|first1=Anne|title=STEM vs. STEAM: Do the Arts Belong?|url=http://www.edweek.org/tm/articles/2014/11/18/ctq-jolly-stem-vs-steam.html|journal=Teacher|date=18 November 2014|publisher=Education Week: Teacher|access-date=6 September 2016}}</ref>
*[[SteamHead]] is a non-profit organization that promotes innovation and accessibility in education, focusing on STEAM fields.
* As part of a $1.5 million Department of Education grant, Wolf Trap's Institute of Education trains and places teaching artists in preschool and kindergarten classrooms. The artists collaborate with the teachers to integrate math and science into the arts.<ref name="pbs">{{cite web|url=https://www.pbs.org/newshour/education/the-movement-to-put-arts-into-stem-education|title=STEAM Ahead: Merging Arts and Science Education|last1=Chen|first1=Kelly|last2=Cheers|first2=Imani|date=31 July 2012|website=[[PBS NewsHour]]|publisher=PBS|access-date=7 March 2015}}</ref>
* Nonprofit organizations focused on closing the digital divide have adopted STEAM frameworks to connect underrepresented communities — particularly Black and Latino youth — with technology education, workforce preparation, and creative arts programs.<ref>{{cite web |title=Healthy Communities |url=https://www.cdc.gov/grand-rounds/pp/2018/20180116-healthy-communities.html |access-date=2026-02-28 |publisher=CDC}}</ref>
